summary.text: Hydrothermal vents are fissures on the seabed from which geothermally heated water discharges, commonly near volcanically active places and mid-ocean ridges.
Chemosynthetic bacteria and archaea around them form the base of a food chain supporting giant tube worms, clams, limpets and shrimp.
Water leaves vents at 60 to 464 °C, far hotter than the roughly 2 °C water around them, and vents are hypothesized to have helped start life.

facts.label: Black smoker depth
facts.value: Most often 2,500 to 3,000 m below the surface

facts.label: Chimney growth
facts.value: As much as 30 cm per day recorded

facts.label: Deepest known site
facts.value: Beebe, at about 5,000 m in the Cayman Trough

items.prompt: Far below the ocean's surface, giant tube worms and clams crowd around a vent. What feeds that community?

options.label: Plankton raining down from sunlit water
Algae growing on the chimneys
Microbes that live on chemicals dissolved in the vent fluid
Fish that migrate there

items.explain: Chemosynthetic bacteria and archaea form the base of the food chain, fueled by chemicals in the vent fluids.

items.prompt: Why do tall chimney stacks form at some vents?

options.label: Sediment from the nearby seafloor is piled up by ocean currents
Minerals dissolved in the hot fluid solidify when it meets near-freezing seawater
Tube worms build them from shells
Cooled lava hardens into columns above the vent

items.explain: When superheated water contacts near-freezing sea water, dissolved minerals precipitate out and add to the height of the stacks.

items.prompt: At about 400 °C a deep vent's water does not simply boil away into steam. Why?

options.label: The high pressure at that depth keeps it liquid or supercritical
The surrounding rock soaks up the heat first
Salt in the water lowers its boiling point
The cold seawater cools it before it can boil

items.explain: Because of high hydrostatic pressure at these depths, water can exist as a liquid or a supercritical fluid at such temperatures.

items.prompt: Why are deep-ocean vents often found along mid-ocean ridges such as the Mid-Atlantic Ridge?

options.label: Plates are pulling apart there and new crust is forming
Plates collide there and grind the rock to powder
Ridges are where the oldest seafloor sits
Ridges are where the ice caps meet the ocean

items.explain: Deep-ocean vents typically form along mid-ocean ridges, where two tectonic plates diverge and new crust is formed.

items.prompt: What makes the clouds from black smokers dark?

options.label: Soot from burning organic matter
Volcanic ash thrown out with the water
Ink-like pigment released by vent animals
Particles with high levels of sulfur-bearing minerals

items.explain: Black smokers emit a cloud of black material, with particles high in sulfur-bearing minerals, or sulfides.

items.prompt: Where does most of the water from a seafloor vent come from?

options.label: Rain that percolated down from the surface
Seawater drawn into the system through faults and porous sediments
Water released by melting magma alone
Groundwater from nearby continents

items.explain: Seafloor vent water is mostly seawater drawn in through faults and porous sediments, plus some magmatic water.
